claims.harm: txindex parallelization causes a 3-13% slowdown on SSDs, and combining a generic shared thread pool with complex out-of-order index synchronization introduces excessive complexity
claims.quote: The txindex parallelization appears to be broken (showing 3-13% slowdowns rather than speedups)... Approach NACK from me.

claims.harm: txindex sync on SSD is ~7% slower than master due to LevelDB write contention across worker threads offsetting parallel digest gains
claims.quote: master was ~7% faster than this PR with 5 workers on an SSD. Maybe we don't enable parallel sync for txindex?

claims.harm: parallel indexing on HDDs causes a 2x slowdown compared to sequential master due to disk seek penalties
claims.quote: observed a slowdown on a HDD compared to master (by a factor 2)... Should it be mentioned in the -indexworkers help

claims.harm: specifying -indexworkers=0 triggers an assertion failure in ThreadPool on startup
claims.quote: -indexworkers=0 is allowed according to the doc, but it will trigger the assert num_workers > 0 in the ThreadPool.

claims.harm: intermittent segfault during index sync caused by worker threads accessing an index Sync() local variable post-destruction
claims.quote: Fwiw I encountered a segfault previously while testing on master on previous PR HEAD
claims.settled_by_quote: There was a very subtle bug on which the worker threads might have accessed an index Sync() local variable post-destruction.

claims.harm: thread pool fuzzer times out after 1608 seconds during thread destruction / joining
claims.quote: It seems to have found something: ... ERROR: libFuzzer: timeout after 1608 seconds
claims.settled_by_quote: Updated with a fuzz test case from @TheCharlatan. Thanks!

claims.harm: taking a reference to a temporary CBlockUndo object at block height 0 causes undefined behavior
claims.quote: I'm not sure this is safe. It looks like if block height is 0 this is taking a reference to a temporary object that will go out scope.
